summary.text: Hassan Nehme is the Republican candidate for the Michigan House of Representatives, District 15, in the November 3, 2026 general election, facing Democrat Jalal Abdallah in a race with no incumbent.
Ballotpedia says he served in the U.S. Army from 2012 to 2016 and is a small business owner.

paragraphs.text: Hassan Nehme was born in Farmington Hills, Michigan, and earned a high school diploma from Crestwood High School, according to Ballotpedia.
He attended Saint Louis University and Henry Ford College.
Nehme ran in the Republican primary for Michigan's 12th Congressional District in 2022, finishing third with 3,196 votes (11.7 percent) behind Steven Elliott and James Hooper.
Ballotpedia lists him among the withdrawn or disqualified Republican candidates for the same seat in 2024.
He advanced unopposed from the 2026 Republican primary for District 15 on August 4, 2026, receiving 2,470 votes.

In a Ballotpedia survey, Nehme listed housing affordability, small-business growth, infrastructure and flooding, education and parental involvement, healthcare access, veterans, public safety and government accountability among his policy interests.
He said he wants to leave behind "stronger neighborhoods, better opportunities for families and young people, more trust in government."
